column1: # 9B gate-fix pilot: validate the resume gate's live latch read (item 6) across CONSECUTIVE runs, and
# measure CPU s-model first lock-on under the PINNED controller for the first time.
# The four consolidation session plans are unchanged; this file is additional.
# Order is deliberate:
#   1 sentinel, the usual first run of a session, and the A3 band check.
#   2 yolov8s CPU, the slowest s-model (sweep: 1.296 Hz, min gap 0.619 s), so the strongest test of the
#     pinned 0.4 to 0.6 s lock-on rule. First CPU s-model run ever done under the pinned controller.
#   3 yolo26n NPU, the fast path immediately after a CPU run: if anything stale survived from run 2 the
#     gate would resume before this run's own latch, so this is the stale-line test.
#   4 yolo26s CPU, the fastest s-model (sweep: 1.567 Hz, min gap 0.576 s, 4 of 332 gaps <= 0.6 s), the
#     marginal case of the same rule.
#   5 yolov11n CPU, the positive control: an n-model at 3.8 Hz, whose gaps are mostly under 0.4 s, so it
#     must lock on and reach. If run 5 fails, the fix is wrong rather than the detector being too slow.
# NPU opens: 1 session-gate start reference + 2 (run 1) + 2 (run 3) + 1 end reference = 6 of the 40 budget.
# Windows come from config/protocol_fx554.json: default 60 s for every row here (no CPU m-model in this plan).
